story.headline: Pogacar equals all-time Tour record
story.summary: Tadej Pogacar won a record-equalling fifth Tour de France, drawing level with Anquetil, Merckx, Hinault and Indurain.
story.display_body: Slovenia's Tadej Pogacar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) sealed his fifth Tour de France on the Champs-Elysees, drawing level with the sport's four all-time greats - Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain - as the only riders to win cycling's biggest race five times. It is his third in a row. As flagged here last week, the contest had effectively closed once his one real threat, two-time winner Jonas Vingegaard, abandoned with a broken collarbone on stage 15; his other rival, Belgium's Remco Evenepoel, finished second overall, 6 minutes 26 seconds back. Pogacar, 27, took five stage wins including a record ascent of Alpe d'Huez.
story.why: Five wins puts Pogacar in the conversation as the greatest cyclist ever - but the reception is telling. He was booed by some fans during the race, less out of dislike than frustration that his dominance has drained the Tour of suspense. That tension - a generational champion whose brilliance makes the event less competitive - is now the sport's central question.

story.headline: Norris wins as Antonelli leads title
story.summary: Lando Norris took McLaren's first win of 2026 at the Hungarian GP as Piastri retired; Kimi Antonelli leads the championship into the summer break.
story.display_body: Lando Norris won the Hungarian Grand Prix for his and McLaren's first victory of the 2026 season - a striking line to write about a team that dominated the sport a year ago. His race-long McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri led the first half after passing Norris at the start, but lost time trapped behind a Carlos Sainz-Fernando Alonso battle (Sainz got a five-second penalty for ignoring blue flags and drifting into Piastri, who raged over team radio), was overcut by Norris in the pits, then retired with a gearbox failure on lap 56. Max Verstappen salvaged second from a difficult weekend; Mercedes' teenager Kimi Antonelli took third after Lewis Hamilton was demoted by a pit-lane speeding penalty.
story.why: A year ago McLaren were the benchmark and Antonelli a rookie; that a Mercedes driver now leads by two clear wins' worth of points, and McLaren celebrated its first win only in late July, is the clearest sign yet that the 2026 regulation reset genuinely reshuffled the grid rather than merely tweaking it.

story.headline: Swiss Super League season opens
story.summary: The 2026-27 Swiss Super League began, St. Gallen beating FCZ 2-1 and Young Boys beating Sion 4-2, both after conceding first.
story.display_body: The 2026-27 Swiss Super League - the country's twelve-team top flight - kicked off this weekend, and the two marquee Sunday fixtures both turned on late comebacks. In front of a sold-out St. Gallen, the hosts trailed to a first-half Umeh Emmanuel goal for Zurich before Lukas Goertler equalised from a worked corner (70') and summer signing Andrin Hunziker deflected in the winner four minutes later for a 2-1 St. Gallen victory. It was a pointed result for FCZ's new coach Marcel Koller - the man who led St. Gallen to their last league title 26 years ago - whose reshaped side created the better first-half chances but left empty-handed. In Bern, Young Boys threw away a 2-0 lead against Sion before Samuel Essende's second-half brace rescued a 4-2 win.
story.why: For most Swiss towns the Super League - not the World Cup that just finished - is the sport that structures the autumn, and the opening weekend already hints at the season's shape: a champion (Thun) nobody expected to defend, a rebuilt Zurich under a returning veteran coach, and a St. Gallen side punching above its weight at home and in Europe.

story.headline: Tagger and Halys land maiden titles
story.summary: Austrian teenager Lilli Tagger won her first WTA title in Prague and France's Quentin Halys his first ATP title in Kitzbuehel.
story.display_body: The post-Wimbledon lull is a quiet, lower-tier stretch of the calendar, but this week delivered two genuine breakthroughs. Austrian teenager Lilli Tagger won the WTA Prague Open for her first career title on the women's tour, beating Ukraine's Daria Snigur 7-6(3), 6-2 on Sunday. A day earlier, France's Quentin Halys took the ATP Generali Open in Kitzbuehel - his maiden ATP Tour title - edging Alexander Bublik 6-4, 7-6(8-6). Neither event carries ranking weight near the top of the game, and there was no Swiss winner this week.
story.why: First titles are the tour's leading indicator - they mark which unseeded names are about to start troubling the seeds at the bigger hard-court events (Canada, Cincinnati, then the US Open) over the next month.

story.headline: Wildfires push 300,000 from homes near Bordeaux
story.summary: Wildfires around Bordeaux forced one of France's largest-ever evacuations, with around 300,000 people moved across France and Spain and a new heatwave forecast from Tuesday.
story.display_body: Wildfires around Bordeaux drove one of the largest evacuations in French history, with around 300,000 people now moved to safety across France and Spain and the flames roughly 15 km from the city. In southwest France the fire in the Gironde has burned more than 19,000 hectares and destroyed about 100 buildings since Wednesday, forcing some 220,000 people from their homes — 55,000 more ordered out around Bordeaux over the weekend, and 31,000 in neighbouring Landes; boats were used to evacuate holidaymakers from the Cap Ferret peninsula. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the blaze turned "extremely violent and unpredictable" overnight, the A63 motorway to Spain is shut over about 60 km, and nearly 100,000 hectares have burned nationwide since January — a historic record. In Spain the government declared a state of emergency around Madrid and in Ávila (where about 47,000 hectares burned), with roughly 90,000 people evacuated according to the interior ministry; El País reports the Madrid, Ávila and Toledo fires have covered some 77,000 hectares in all. A new heatwave with temperatures up to 40°C is forecast from Tuesday 28 July, threatening to worsen the fight.
story.why: This is the sharp escalation of a fire emergency running across France, Spain and Italy since 23 July — the direct threat to Bordeaux, a metropolis of about 850,000, and the incoming heat push it well beyond the earlier evacuations.

story.headline: Iran vows retaliation over Caspian Sea strike
story.summary: Iran summoned Ukraine's envoy and threatened reprisals after a Ukrainian strike killed a sailor on an Iranian Caspian Sea vessel, as a US-Iran strike pause held a second day.
story.display_body: Iran warned Ukraine it will retaliate for a deadly strike on an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, opening a new front that links the Russia–Ukraine war to the recent US–Israel conflict with Iran. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday 26 July that the Ukrainian attack the day before — which Iran says caused the ship to explode, killing one sailor and injuring several — "cannot go unanswered" and violated the UN Charter, and he accused Israel of provoking it to "drag Europe into its war." Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his forces had hit "vessels used in military cargo shipments involving Iran, as well as a warship" in long-range strikes, and accused Russia of feeding Iran satellite imagery of US facilities in the Gulf. Iran has summoned Ukraine's chargé d'affaires in Tehran, and a senior lawmaker said early Monday that Kyiv "may soon come to understand that Iran does not let actions go unanswered." Separately, the United States and Iran held off on fresh strikes for a second straight day, and oil prices eased.
story.why: Kyiv striking an Iranian ship — over Tehran's supply of Shahed drones to Moscow since 2022 — risks pulling Iran directly into the Ukraine war just as a fragile pause in the US–Iran fighting takes hold.

story.headline: Berlin Pride attacker shot dead by police
story.summary: German police killed the suspect in Saturday's Berlin Pride van-ramming, treated as an Islamist terrorist attack by the interior minister; one person died and 29 were injured.
story.display_body: German police shot dead the suspect in Saturday night's Berlin Pride van-ramming attack, which Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said authorities are treating as an "Islamist terrorist attack." The suspect was killed in a police operation on Sunday 26 July after, police said, attacking officers with a bladed weapon; Dobrindt said there was no indication of a further threat. One person was killed and 29 injured — a higher toll than the 16 reported the day before — when the attacker drove a van into a crowd in Tiergarten Park, near the Christopher Street Day parade, one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ celebrations. Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged marchers "not to be intimidated," and the Brandenburg Gate was lit in the colours of the Pride flag for a candlelit vigil.
story.why: The "Islamist terrorist" classification is the interior minister's characterisation and the investigation is early, but a deadly attack on a Pride event has already prompted German calls for tighter security.

story.headline: Brazil recalls ambassador after Milei insults Lula
story.summary: Brazil recalled its ambassador to Argentina after President Milei called Lula a 'convict' and 'thief' at a Bolsonaro campaign event in São Paulo.
story.display_body: Brazil recalled its ambassador to Argentina on Sunday 26 July after President Javier Milei insulted President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Brazilian soil. At a São Paulo campaign event the day before for Flávio Bolsonaro — son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro and a likely 2026 challenger to Lula — Milei called the Brazilian leader a "convict," a "delinquent" and a "thief" without naming him, and derided Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes as "bald trash." Brazil's foreign ministry said there was "no precedent for a foreign president, on national territory, to hurl insults" at its head of state and institutions, and also summoned Argentina's ambassador.
story.why: Argentina and Brazil are each other's main regional trading partners and the core of the Mercosur bloc; a personal rupture between their presidents, tied to Argentina's libertarian right backing Brazil's far right, strains an already fraying relationship.

story.headline: Pakistan monsoon floods kill 107
story.summary: Pakistan's monsoon death toll since late June reached at least 107 with 344 injured, and authorities warned of more heavy rain across Punjab this week.
story.display_body: Pakistan's monsoon death toll since late June reached at least 107, with 344 injured, and authorities warned of more heavy rain this week. The National Disaster Management Authority said Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has recorded the most deaths (55), followed by Punjab (36), and that more than half were caused by house or roof collapses. In Punjab, an irrigation official described "a vast area of around 400 sq km" now under water across the Lahore and Gujranwala divisions, calling it "an inland sea"; Lahore has set up at least 17 flood-relief camps.

story.headline: Swiss crews join French wildfire fight
story.summary: Thirty-four Romand firefighters deployed to the Gironde and Switzerland's army will send two Super Puma helicopters to fight the French wildfires.
story.display_body: Thirty-four firefighters from French-speaking Switzerland — mostly Geneva, with crews from Vaud and Neuchâtel — arrived in the Gironde late on Saturday 25 July and worked through the night west of Cestas, about 10 km from Bordeaux's ring road, saving much of a solar-panel farm before the wind turned; further rotations are planned through 1 August. Separately, after France requested aircraft, the Swiss defence department (DDPS) decided to deploy two Super Puma helicopters to the Var department, expected to leave on Tuesday 28 July alongside a small humanitarian-aid rapid-response team.
story.why: It is a concrete cross-border civil-protection commitment, and — with Switzerland's own forests parched — a marker of how the same drought conditions now stretch Alpine-region emergency services.

story.headline: Swiss customs office cuts management posts
story.summary: Switzerland's federal customs office (OFDF) announced a restructuring cutting about 25 management posts and reverting to a pre-2023 regional structure.
story.display_body: Director Pascal Lüthi, in post since January 2024, told staff the agency's 23 "local levels" — created under former director Christian Bock, whose contract was terminated in May 2023 — will become 16 "customs posts," and its six regions (including "Douane Ouest," covering Geneva, Vaud and Valais) will revert to four from 1 August 2026, with new directorates in place from 1 January 2027 and a transition lasting until end-2031. Current managers must reapply for their jobs, which some staff fear will be used to remove inconvenient cadres; the office says it aims to find an internal solution for everyone affected. Reporting is drawn from CH Media titles (Aargauer Zeitung, Luzerner Zeitung, St. Galler Tagblatt).
